In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cutaneous lesions are significantly more frequent in nocardiosis non-survivors than in survivors.
the presence of cutaneous lesions is associated with a higher mortality rate of Nocardia infection in patients with CTSs.
cutaneous lesions as a manifestation of disseminated disease are a risk factor for mortality in patients with nocardiosis and underlying CTDs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with CTD who have cutaneous lesions should receive prophylactic TMP-SMX.
nocardiosis should be included in the differential diagnosis of patients with CTD and cutaneous lesions.
cutaneous lesions as a sign of disseminated nocardiosis in CTDs patients should raise the awareness of physicians to the risk of nocardiosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nocardiosis is an under-recognized complication of CTDs and clinicians should consider it in the differential diagnoses.
clinicians should be vigilant of cutaneous lesions in patients with CTCs, and should consider nocardiosis as one of the differential diagnoses.
